documents.title: The core motion language for every style
documents.content:
# Motion language: the reusable foundation

This is the default craft system for After Effects Studio. It carries the production decisions developed in Joe Benscoter's Content pipeline into projects with different subjects, brands and aspect ratios. Read it at the beginning of every motion-design task. The user's brief chooses the look; this language determines how to reason about the animation.

## 1. Start with an operation the viewer can understand

Describe a scene using an active verb and an observable before/after: a message is carried into a draft; a pile is scanned into an organized set; a container opens to reveal its structure; a value changes as material leaves. “Make screenshots fluid,” “add premium motion,” or “animate three cards” does not yet describe the idea.

Choose a specific subject, a primary action and a payoff. The strongest candidate is often already in the narration or product workflow. Start literal before inventing an unrelated metaphor. If source material already contains the action, compose and emphasize that evidence; do not bury it under decorative graphics.

## 2. Give attention a stable object

Choose the scene's star: an identifiable object, label, piece of evidence or character. It can leave and return; its return should pay off an earlier setup. Keep its identity legible while the environment changes. A recognizable object crossing a boundary communicates continuity more clearly than a sequence of unrelated cards.

A recurring star is a storytelling technique, not a requirement to add a mascot to every project. A chart's value, a real reply, or a product silhouette can be the star. Keep tiny bright characters away from evidence and reading areas.

## 3. Construct, act, resolve

Build a picture from related parts over time. Establish the surface or guide, reveal structure, introduce the hero, add its meaningful detail, change its state, then hold the result. Supporting movements overlap without competing for attention. Repeating the same entrance on a collection of finished pictures does not implement this language.

For explanatory construction sequences, retain the detailed measured grammar in `construction`: line first, material resolution, delayed accent, a distinct snap, a shared hand-off. For a slower title or cinematic product shot, retain causal staging and hierarchy while changing density and timing. Universal means the mechanism transfers; it does not mean reducing it to “use easing.”

## 4. Make movement earn its place

Translation carries; rotation reveals; scale changes emphasis or space; occlusion establishes depth; exact contact completes an action; a camera move connects two ideas. Name that purpose in the brief. If the movement has no subject or outcome, revise it before adding keys.

Separate object motion from camera motion. Fast detail can happen inside a readable, stable composition. The camera has its own slower rhythm. Do not attach a new zoom to every spoken word. Selective stillness and restrained drift are both valid holds; state which you intend.

## 5. Design the middle and the landing

Compose start, action and payoff poses for the hardest passage. Include the actual intermediate overlap and destination registration. The middle is where duplicate text, clipping, ambiguous depth and unexplained arcs hide. Prose alone rarely reveals these problems.

For a source-to-destination transfer, specify source rectangle, pivot, trajectory, scale, rotation, destination bounds and exactly when the source copy disappears. If the source is evidence, preserve its meaning and identity. Do not animate a user instruction into a supposed product result or a draft into proof of a sent message.

## 6. Material quality and precision work together

Native AE owns exact type, data, paths, masks, keyframes, UI and compositing. Supplied, licensed or generated art can supply sophisticated surfaces and recognizable physical objects. These assets should be prepared for motion: clean alpha, consistent viewpoint, no baked shadow when AE owns the lighting, and separate moving pieces.

Do not substitute a rectangle for a requested premium physical object and call it finished. A native document, chart, circuit or intentionally geometric diagram is a legitimate subject. If the brief requires a polished product asset and none is available, resolve that dependency or show a clearly labeled blocking study. See `assets-depth`.

## 7. Typography carries structure

Use a held section title to establish the idea when that fits the format. Essential words survive long enough to read. Subtitles support speech; they should not compete with title, proof and hero for the same area. Long copy calls for a layout decision, not indiscriminate shrinking. Measure rendered bounds at delivery size and during camera pushes.

## 8. Critique the artifact and revise the brief when needed

Build a representative difficult section before scaling a new visual system across the whole piece. Include an ordinary explanatory beat as well as a hero or transition: one excellent moment does not prove the rest. Inspect rendered frames, dense transition samples and a playable clip. Technical success, visual quality and the user's approval are separate claims.

When feedback reveals a wrong visual idea, rewrite the scene brief from the reference and intent. Repeatedly patching the named symptom can preserve the wrong design for several rounds. Capture accepted techniques with exact parameters and evidence in the user's project so future work benefits.

## Default reading path

Read `production-workflow`, then the relevant modules: `construction`, `camera-continuity`, `assets-depth`, `type-evidence`, `reference-study`, `failure-atlas`, and `worked-scenes`. Before building, create the portable brief described in `brief-template`. Before delivery, apply `quality`. These are included files, available through ae_library or directly under library; they never require the original repo.

documents.title: Portable cold-start production workflow
documents.content:
# Portable production workflow

This process uses the user's request and assets plus the plugin. It does not expect Joe's Content checkout, personal fonts, footage or a preexisting MASTER rig.

## 1. Orient and specify

Read `motion-language` and inspect the AE host/project. Identify the target project, format, duration, message, evidence, narration, available assets and reference. Infer ordinary choices from the request. Ask only for information that changes the result or an asset that is genuinely required. Never close or save over unrelated unsaved work.

For an empty project, create the needed compositions and native layers explicitly. Don't call house rig functions assuming JOE, BOARD, CAMERA or GRAIN exists. `motion-jsx` is portable; `house-jsx` and `joeb-motion-jsx` are optional integrations with declared dependencies.

## 2. Establish the visual operation

Use the brief template. Define start/action/payoff for each section, the star, material treatment, typography roles, factual sources, camera purpose, frame timings and hand-off. Read the actual available assets before naming them. The detailed language is the default foundation even when the requested look is completely different from JoeB.

If the user provides a visual reference, measure a relevant short shot using `reference-study`. Transfer its mechanism into an original design. Use references and examples to make decisions, not as decoration in a moodboard.

## 3. Test the hard passage and an ordinary beat

For a new look, compose start/action/payoff poses and build a small representative native section. Include the difficult hand-off and a normal proof/explanation beat. This checks whether the visual system sustains more than one impressive moment. When the user asks for iterative direction, show this section for feedback. When authorized to complete autonomously, self-review and continue; don't insert an unrequested approval stop.

## 4. Build in coherent sections

Create versioned scripts with scene ownership prefixes. Preserve approved layers/assets and rebuild only the intended sections. Parent at rest, set coordinate spaces, create actual background layers, and inspect text bounds. Fetch schemas from the native operation catalog; legacy cloud bridge limitations are not the native API contract.

Record what actually changed and compare the live project to that expectation. Script failures and timeouts mean the visual state is uncertain. Inspect before retrying. Do not render a stale pre-build project and mistake it for the new version.

## 5. Review and correct

Apply `failure-atlas` and `quality`. Inspect the native render across start, action, maximum overlap, hold and transition. Use a contact sheet for temporal coverage and full-size frames for edges/type. Review denser frame strips around fast hand-offs. Use a playable clip for speed, sound, camera rhythm and VO sync. If playback is unavailable, explicitly leave those checks open.

Name the weak part and fix its cause. If the idea is wrong, revise the brief. If a rendered middle pose fails, fix the trajectory/stack, not only the endpoint. Technical pass is not taste approval. Don't claim a user has approved something because automated checks passed.

## 6. Deliver editability and a verified file

Save intentionally, gather referenced assets, retain native editable type/shapes/keyframes, and export the requested format. Use an existing suitable render template or discover actual installed options. Verify output metadata and complete decode. Check the delivered copy matches the verified export when copying elsewhere. Report remaining dependencies and unperformed checks.

## 7. Preserve reusable discoveries

In the project, record the accepted operation, exact timings/curves, assets, implementation pitfalls and evidence. Distinguish proven user preference from a hypothesis. A fix becomes a reusable recipe when it works across builds or the user explicitly adopts it. Don't silently mutate global memory or the installed plugin during ordinary production.

documents.title: Portable scene and production brief
documents.content:
# Portable motion brief

Use before building a new piece. Scale length to the task and keep it in the user's project for context-independent resumption.

## Project

- Viewer takeaway:
- Duration / aspect / resolution / fps:
- Style, material, palette roles and available fonts:
- Exact target AE project/comp; preservation of unrelated work:
- Inputs: files, narration/transcript, reference, factual data:
- Delivery: editable project/assets, review clip, master spec:
- Missing dependencies and resolution:

## Scene N — start/end

- Operation (active verb, before → action → after):
- Star / stable anchor / identity across the scene:
- Title and other reading jobs:
- Start/action/payoff poses and hardest overlap bounds:
- Inspected assets; native/supplied/generated/illustrative/evidence status:
- Material, depth, shadow, occlusion:
- Events: frame/time, change, subject, target, spoken cue, duration/ease:
- Semantic turn/snap; accent response:
- Camera subject, destination, duration, hold and purpose; or intentionally static:
- Incoming/outgoing hand-off, visibility boundaries, carried objects:
- Exact on-screen numbers/text and sources; illustrative labels:
- Material assumptions or choices:

## Build/review

- Representative section: hardest hand-off plus ordinary explanation/proof.
- Ownership prefixes and reusable controls.
- Check times: first-readable, action peak, overlap, hold, seam neighborhood.
- Risks: text fit, coverage, alpha, duplicates, continuity.
- Playback/VO/audio checks and anything unavailable here.
- Expected project state, stale-build detection and delivery checks.

Event count diagnoses a chosen fast construction style; it is not a mandatory quota for a slow title or quiet proof. Every scene needs a meaningful change or an intentional hold. If feedback changes the operation, revise this brief before layering local fixes.

documents.title: Detailed construction timing and gesture grammar
documents.content:
# Construction, timing and gesture grammar

Adapted from the October 6 motion playbook and the two house-polish scene scripts. The numbers below preserve the useful craft detail. They describe a proven fast explanatory style at 30 fps, not all genres. Convert frame values using the actual comp frame rate. If choosing a different pace, write the reason and preserve the sequence of attention.

## Anatomy of the explanatory section

A 2.5–6 second section holds one visual idea. The original grammar used a held title, one evolving picture, roughly 12–16 overlapping events, and a new small event every 6–10 frames. An event is a visible addition or state change, not a keyframe. Don't hit the quota by adding meaningless flashes. A documentary proof hold or slow title may deliberately use fewer events.

Order the construction: baseline / guide → outline → hero material → selection / detail → action → consequence → reading hold → hand-off. Let the next supporting action begin before the previous one finishes. Start the object already moving instead of revealing a static finished picture and then animating it.

## Easing, explicitly

| Function | Out influence | In influence | Starting duration at 30fps |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Settle into place | 28 | 85 | 13–15 frames for the larger arrival |
| Deliberate travel / fill | 82 | 82 | Fit the state change and narration |
| Accelerating exit / collapse | 75 | 12 | Often 3–7 frames per gesture |
| Pop impulse | linear | linear | 3 frames, followed by a spring |

The pipeline's mining found one transform property per layer in 81% of measured transform entrances; offsets commonly lived between components rather than Position + Scale + Opacity on every layer. Use this as a complexity warning, not an absolute ban on multi-property action. Sample: 307 unique moves from 66 files across template packs; pack duplication/style concentration limits generalization. No reach or audience claim follows from those counts.

For the spring, sample incoming velocity just before the last key and add `v * 0.05 * sin(2.6 * t * 2pi) / exp(6.5 * t)`. The measured peak was around 17% of travel. These values are included in `motion-jsx`. For a picture resting at 24% scale, animate multiples of 24, not a reset to 100. Key linear impulses explicitly.

## Stagger and anticipation

- Handles and small badges: 2–3 frames apart; adjacent title lines: about 2 frames.
- A many-object cascade follows the sweep's actual crossing time, rather than a generic delay by index.
- Separate objects: 0.15–0.2 seconds as a starting point.
- Anticipation stays smaller than the action: the reference leaned about 25px or lifted a dot 18px. Scale distance with composition size; don't turn anticipation into a second main event.
- A VO-linked object often starts 0.1–0.25s before its word so it lands on the word. Transcribe the actual locked audio and check the word onset; draft script timing is not sufficient.

## Line → material → accent

Native trim paths, crop marks, guide lines and handles create an intelligible construction. In the original, guides ran beyond the stage at 1.8px with a 9/7 dash-gap; scale line weight for the output resolution. Keep construction crisp. Material may be a well-made cut-out or native geometry appropriate to the subject. Bring the accent on the semantic turn, then cut away construction on the snap.

An outlined generic icon is not equivalent to a premium material object. The pipeline improved when asset design and motion design were both addressed; adding better easing to weak artwork did not solve it.

## Collapse and removal

Quick delete: scale relative to the resting size toward `[112%,4%]` over 3 frames, then end the layer. Longer collapse: flatten to a sliver (4f), close to a dot (3f), wind up (2f), drop (4f). Retain the spatial center so the viewer reads one transformation. A receiving slot can react with one small spring. Hold the empty/clean state long enough for the consequence to register.

## Shared whip hand-off

Outgoing y offsets over seven frames: `[0,-8,-26,-66,-150,-430,-760]`.
Incoming offsets over eight frames: `[640,300,118,56,26,11,4,0]`.
One outgoing frame carries about 40% of the travel. Introduce the new scene on that fast frame and preserve the travel direction. These are sampled positions; use linear interpolation between samples. Scale distances to cover the current stage. Test the transition at native frame rate, including motion-blur shutter samples.

## Scene structure

Group related layers beneath a dedicated scene null, establish its anchor and position before parenting, and key it only after placement. Children retain their own internal event timing while the carrier performs the hand-off. A traveling star that bridges sections must outlive the first section's outPoint. Keep typography screen-locked or scene-locked intentionally; do not accidentally inherit a whip.

documents.title: Visual review and delivery checks
documents.content:
# A render is the evidence

## Design and motion review

Inspect full-frame captures at the beginning, build, peak overlap, hold and hand-off. Use contact sheets for temporal continuity and full-resolution stills for type and edges. Check the exported file, not only AE's viewer. Look for:

- A clear visual message with hierarchy and enough reading time.
- No unintended clipping, collisions, blank frames, stale scenes or offscreen essential information.
- Consistent light, shadows, material, palette, edge quality and perspective.
- Motions with a cause and a destination; appropriately weighted easing; clean parenting and anchor behavior.
- Readable type and correct glyphs at phone size; no font fallback or template copy left behind.
- Exact user-supplied numbers, product facts and UI text. Label illustrative data.
- Proper alpha/key edges, no green spill, wrong blend mode or double shadows.
- Seam continuity, source-media completeness and no obsolete asset paths.

Contact sheets cannot prove playback rhythm, sound balance or lip sync. Play the export at speed for those checks. If this interface cannot play audiovisual content, report that limitation separately from inspected frames.

## Technical delivery

Save the intended version and include linked assets. Preserve editable type, shapes, masks and keyframes. Render a review encode and the requested master codec. Verify duration, resolution, frame rate, streams and file size with ffprobe when available. Decode the full video with ffmpeg using `-v error -i <file> -f null -`; an exit-zero decode detects corruption, not visual polish. Compare hashes when copying a verified master to another destination.

Use `scripts/verify-export.mjs <file>` for metadata plus a full decode. It exits nonzero on failure and explicitly requires ffmpeg and ffprobe. Check the requested spec against its report.

## Handoff

Report what changed, the project and render paths, evidence reviewed, and any missing checks. Keep technical pass, craft judgment and user approval distinct. Record accepted new recipes in the project with exact timings and reference frames. Never claim publication, audience performance or approval from a clean export alone.

documents.title: Production failures causes and corrections
documents.content:
# Failures that shaped the language

These are practical diagnoses from actual motion production and plugin validation. Use the symptom → cause → correction mapping during review. Historical Content cases are mapped in `source-map.json`; newer validation cases are recorded in dated quality reports. Historical quotes, business data and user media are not needed to apply the lessons.

| Symptom | What went wrong | Correction and evidence to inspect |
|---|---|---|
| A polished slide deck instead of motion graphics | Finished generic pictures entered, then parked | Design construction, action, consequence and hand-off; inspect a whole section at speed |
| Better easing still looks cheap | Artwork remained an outlined stand-in for a material object | Fix asset design/viewpoint/light as well as choreography |
| A generated video is visually rich but uncontrollable | Precise changes were baked into the clip | Keep exact type, UI, object relationships and motion native; use prepared assets for material |
| One impressive hero, weak ordinary scenes | Effort was concentrated in the showcase moment | Test a routine evidence beat and transition before scaling production |
| Repeated boxes explain unrelated sentences | The same kit prop replaced literal visual ideas | Give each sentence an acting picture inside a coherent analogy world |
| Camera feels jerky | Word-by-word stop-start keys | One purposeful longer move per transition; preserve reading holds |
| Camera push clips type | Static auto-fit ignored camera bounds | Test the widest line through maximum zoom and clamp/recompose the camera |
| One-frame ghost at scene change | Visibility and camera jump were not frame-exact | Quantize the seam, account for shutter sampling, inspect f-2…f+2 |
| Blank/black ground in export | Comp background was mistaken for a rendered layer | Add a real background with adequate overscan |
| Image pop changes the intended size | Helper reset scale to 100 instead of the asset's resting scale | Animate multiples of the measured base scale |
| Child jumps or grows after parenting | Parenting at the wrong current time preserves the wrong world transform | Parent at rest and set local transforms intentionally |
| A null moves but the visual stack is wrong | Parenting was mistaken for layer order | Move child layers explicitly; inspect occlusion in rendered frames |
| Source and destination show duplicate text | End state was visible underneath the traveling copy | Hide one copy until a matched registration hand-off |
| Multiply still leaves a pale rectangle | Transparent precomp had no intended backing surface | Inspect alpha and backing inside the precomp, then composite on the real ground |
| Foreground object looks pasted on a container | Front rim never occluded the emerging content | Use rear body and masked front faces around the moving object |
| A line lands in the wrong place | Shape path coordinates and layer position were both offset | Choose local or comp coordinates and set the shape transform accordingly |
| A traced guide meets an image at its endpoints but bows away in the middle | The path was drawn from a plausible silhouette instead of measured source geometry | Sample the source feature along its length, map those points through the image layer's scale and position, then inspect dense rendered overlap frames before approving the hand-off |
| Property operations fail after adding a sibling | Indexed property handle was invalidated | Re-fetch the property by stable path after additions |
| A skipped or old layer stays visible | Creation happened before a continue; layer span was never set | Remove skipped creations and check in/out points on every owned layer |
| Later setup extends every caption to the end | Blanket duration reset affected scene/caption layers | Scope setup to base rig layers and preserve content spans |
| Imported footage shows yesterday's pixels | Source cache retained a reused filename | Use a new versioned file or explicitly reload and verify |
| A clip's entrance drifts after offsetting it | startTime moved animation keys along with media | Separate media timing with a precomp/time remap or rebuild key times |
| UI is technically present but unreadable | Entire desktop was squeezed into a small card | Crop to relevant controls and measure text at final output size |
| Light background reveals key residue | Dark preview hid matte defects | Inspect edges on the actual delivery ground; remeasure screen/spill |
| “Library asset” differs from the brief | Decision relied on catalog prose | Open/render the asset before naming it |
| Review export shows no recent edits | Build failed or connection dropped; stale project was rendered | Read back created IDs/counts and verify expected state before export |
| Patching does not approach the reference | Each note was treated as a local effect request | Re-measure reference, rewrite visual operations, rebuild a representative passage |

## Rejected shortcuts

Layer count, key count, a dense event schedule, an error-free build and a successful export are not independent evidence of taste. A still cannot establish camera rhythm or audio sync. An approval of one scene does not approve an entire production or publication. Keep those distinctions in the handoff.

## Script stops on spatial tangents

A visually 2D layer can expose a three-component Position property. A hardcoded two-value tangent then throws midway through an additive build. Gate spatial methods explicitly on TwoD_SPATIAL/ThreeD_SPATIAL (isSpatial alone proved insufficient in this host test), then inspect `prop.value.length` and create a zero vector of that length; spatial temporal easing still uses one ease object. Retain the partial comp identity, inspect it, and remove only confirmed owned work before retrying. This was reproduced in local AE 26.5 testing of a fresh-context generated script.

documents.title: Native AE scripting and build pitfalls
documents.content:
# AE implementation notes

ExtendScript uses ES3: var, function expressions, ordinary loops and concatenation. The runtime supplies JSON utilities and AE helpers, but a standalone JSX file may not. Return a small JSON-serializable result with created IDs/counts and useful readbacks. Add breadcrumbs for long scripts. Avoid app alerts and modal dialogs.

- Before calling spatial methods, gate on `propertyValueType === PropertyValueType.TwoD_SPATIAL || propertyValueType === PropertyValueType.ThreeD_SPATIAL`; avoid relying on truthiness of `isSpatial` alone. Use dimension-matched easing arrays for ordinary TwoD/ThreeD properties and a single ease object for spatial and scalar properties.
- Inspect spatial property dimensionality from the host, even for a visually 2D layer. Layer Position can expose three-component values; build zero tangent vectors from `prop.value.length` for `setSpatialTangentsAtKey`, not a hardcoded `[0,0]`. Spatial temporal easing uses one `KeyframeEase` per key; that does not imply one- or two-component spatial tangent vectors. Validate these separately.
- New layers are added on top. Use explicit moveBefore/moveAfter when stacking matters. Shape groups have their own draw order; render overlaps.
- Adding a sibling to an indexed property group may invalidate property references. Reacquire handles after additions.
- Parent while the null is at rest; never parent to zero scale. Set parent anchor/position intentionally. Normal parenting preserves world transform at that moment; set local coordinates afterwards if needed.
- Use sourceRectAtTime to size and align actual text. Source Text position is a baseline, not a top-left corner. Test variable font instances and glyph availability.
- Native scripting can set startTime, inPoint and outPoint. Old cloud bridge limitations on time sliding do not apply to this runtime.
- For masks use match names (Mask Expansion is ADBE Mask Offset). Trim Path End stays within 0..100. Re-fetch properties rather than holding stale references across additions.
- Use named effects/match names discovered from the installed host. Custom effect UI parameters are not always scriptable. Apply a valid .ffx preset when a custom LUT picker cannot be set; isolate selection first.
- Import local assets after checking existence and decoding them. New filenames avoid stale footage cache after re-encoding. Verify duration, alpha interpretation, frame rate and color space.
- Use scene-specific prefixes for idempotent rebuilds. Remove only layers owned by that scene; never bulk-remove a user's project to make a demo repeatable.
- Color-managed frame captures can use temporary layers and calibration comps. For a strict inspection-only session use AE_MCP_READONLY=1 and review any colorWarning.
- A native render can block AE. Use intentional render settings, one controller at a time, and a timeout appropriate to the job. A timeout is uncertain completion, not permission to resubmit.

## House library integration

The optional `house-jsx` and `joeb-motion-jsx` are real extracted pipeline code. They require a MASTER composition with the documented JoeB rig, correct fonts, media and AES_HOUSE_CONFIG paths. They are not a blank-project template. Use `motion-jsx` for independent scenes. Read `joeb-preset` before selecting these helpers.
